gaps.sentence: The winner, ___ was only seventeen, broke the championship record.
gaps.hint: person as subject after a comma
gaps.explanation: The clause adds extra information about a person, so 'who' is required and 'that' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: Have you met the couple ___ son is in your class?
gaps.hint: the son belongs to the couple
gaps.explanation: 'Whose son' means 'their son'; the possessive relative 'whose' is required.

gaps.sentence: This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which' and needs no preposition; 'the hotel which we stayed' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: His latest film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject pronoun for the film; 'that' never appears in non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: This is the beach ___ we used to play as children.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' introduces place information; 'we used to play' already has a subject and object, so 'which' is impossible.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.
